ideas: What the skill is and why you needed it
How it has changed your work

phrases.meaning: in a situation that feels uncomfortable
learning by trying and making mistakes

model: The skill I'd like to talk about is public speaking, or more specifically, giving presentations to clients. When I joined my current company as a junior consultant, I was really shy, and I'd never had to present anything to more than a few people. But in my job you have to explain your ideas to clients almost every week, so it was a steep learning curve. At first, it took me completely out of my comfort zone. In meetings I'd hardly speak up, and when I did present, I read everything from the slides. Over the last two years, though, I've been working on it quite seriously. I've watched lots of talks online to see how good speakers hold people's attention, and I've volunteered to present at our monthly team meetings, just for practice. A lot of it was trial and error. I tried telling a short story at the start, using fewer words on the slides and pausing more, and slowly I got the hang of it. My manager has also given me honest feedback, which has really helped to build my confidence. These days it's become almost second nature. I've led several big pitches this year, and we've won two new clients. Honestly, I still get a bit nervous, but I've learned that nerves just mean I care about doing it well.
